value: The nationwide ground stop was cancelled at 8:16 PM ET Friday (FAA Advisory 005). At a Saturday 10:30 AM ET DOT briefing with FAA Administrator Bedford, Duffy said the outage began while contractor L3Harris was switching lines from copper to fiber at a remote FAA site, and a router involved in the work flooded the network; officials have not determined whether the router was faulty or the contractor erred. DOT's written release says the router made over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds; L3Harris says it is supporting the FAA investigation. Officials say there is no sign of a cyberattack. Bedford says the FAA routinely swaps Cisco 600 routers for Juniper routers. The FAA's Nov. 15 written Q&A names the two sites: a radio site in El Dorado, Ark., where L3Harris was deploying a new router, and a radar site in Amarillo, Texas; root cause is still under investigation. The WSJ reports the El Dorado router is a Juniper (Reported). House T&I Democrats expect Bedford at an early December hearing (no date yet). Saturday cancellations topped 6,000.

The national ground stop was cancelled at 8:16 PM ET (Advisory 005), all at once, and by 1:27 AM ET Saturday the last airline-requested hub stop was gone; the FAA summary lists no ground stops. At the White House briefing (~8:35 PM ET), officials gave a cause on the record, reported by Reuters, BBC, the LA Times and Aviation Week: Duffy said legacy analog TDM switches and routers carrying ATC voice and radar data were overloaded with data and began giving inconsistent data at 3:36 PM ET, so the FAA shut the system down; radar and communications were never fully lost. Mullin said new equipment being added was overwhelming the older system, that there is "zero evidence" so far of a cyberattack or rogue AI though neither is ruled out, that it "appears this was mechanically driven," and that the NSA is assisting DHS. AvWeb quotes Duffy saying SMART is not connected to STARS or ERAM and that "There's no possible way SMART would have impacted what happened"; a SMART role stays unconfirmed because Reuters has Mullin saying a rogue AI is not fully ruled out. No official transcript or written FAA report is posted, and the FAA newsroom still says only "communication issues." Saturday at the 10:30 AM ET DOT briefing, Duffy named the trigger on the record: L3Harris copper-to-fiber work at a remote FAA site, with a router involved in the work flooding the network (Yahoo News; AInvest). Still not named: the specific site; not determined: whether the router was faulty or the contractor erred. Reuters, citing two airline officials, says the affected network is the L3Harris-overseen one; L3Harris has not commented. A Saturday Hindustan Times explainer, citing Bloomberg, says some equipment was already running over capacity and that L3Harris has been asked to diagnose the overload; those details stay Reported/unconfirmed. CBS (an update caused a reboot and crash) and Bloomberg (the FBI is looking at a software update) also remain sourced reports, not confirmed. The Air Current, citing airline sources, reports the outage was first noticed at Chicago Center, then Boston, Washington, New York and Minneapolis in rapid succession — reported, not an official log. A circulating claim that NWS/NEXRAD weather radar went down nationwide is debunked; a few airport terminal Doppler radars had brief dropouts, and FAA ATC radar data was intermittent because it rides the overloaded telecom network. On funding: $12.5 billion was already approved in July 2025; Duffy and Vought renewed a $30.1 billion request Friday morning (about $10.1 billion ATC tech, $2 billion towers, $18 billion airports) and Duffy raised the public ask to $50 billion after the outage. House T&I will "thoroughly review" the stop; Sen. Cantwell, Sen. Duckworth and Rep. Lieu have pressed for answers or hearings; no hearing date, NTSB or Inspector General review has been announced. Saturday morning, Duffy said it is safe to fly; the 10:30 AM ET briefing with FAA Administrator Bedford took place, and coverage so far reports no NTSB/IG review, hearing date, center-by-center detail or new SMART statement.
